messages:
Carol: RFC follow-up — thinking about exposing a per-request 'quality_budget' as an API knob to control precision/quant tradeoffs at call time. Example payload:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"prompt\": \"summarize...\",
  \"quality_budget\": 0.75   // 0.0 = cheapest/lowest-fidelity, 1.0 = highest-fidelity
}
```

Tej: I like the ergonomics. Quick Qs: how does this map to pricing? Do we bill proportional to budget (e.g., cost = base_cost * budget) or keep billing unchanged and just expose QoS? :thinking:

Vikram: runtime-wise the big complexity is per-token precision switching + cache/kv compatibility. If a request arrives with budget 0.6 but the KV cache entries were populated at 0.9 fidelity, we need a deterministic downgrade path or re-decoding. Otherwise outputs will mismatch or cache hit semantics break.

Carol: good point. Proposal sketch:
- quality_budget maps to a ranked set of precision lanes (1.0 -> fp8/int8 lane, 0.5 -> int8/4bit lane, 0.0 -> aggressive 4-bit+pruning)
- runtime will pick highest lane <= budget. Cache entries carry a "lane_fingerprint" (small tag) and include a compatibility vector.
- cache hit allowed only if lane_fingerprint <= requested_lane (i.e., cached fidelity >= requested fidelity allowed). If cached fidelity > requested, we allow using it but mark result as "overfidelity_used" (affects cost accounting).

Priya: billing surface still fuzzy. If we allow overfidelity_used we should credit customer with cheaper unit price, or charge actual compute. UX surprises are bad. Two options:
1) Bill actual compute performed (precise but variable for customers)
2) Bill by requested budget but include a low-likelihood surcharge when runtime had to upgrade fidelity for correctness

Tej: Also SLA concerns: if budget low and we pick low-fidelity lane, that could increase hallucinations for some prompts. Do we force an opt-in checkbox per-tenant that allows serving below a safety baseline? Otherwise we may need a per-endpoint minimum_quality.

Vikram: Implementation notes for runtime:
- Add `lane_fingerprint` to KV cache metadata (8-bit tag).
- During decode, maintain tokenwise lane state. We will only change lanes at attention block boundaries to keep KV indexing sane.
- For batching, group by requested_lane; if a mix comes in, use hybrid scheduling: low-lane requests batched together, but if a high-lane request comes we can preemptively run it or fallback some low-lane items to a different GPU pool.

Carol: UX rules:
- Default: endpoints have `min_quality` (set by owner). API `quality_budget` cannot go below that.
- If a customer requests a budget above 1.0 -> clamp. below 0.0 -> clamp.
- Add response header `x-quality-used: 0.65` and `x-quality-source: requested|runtime-upgrade|cache-hit-overfidelity` so customers can reconcile quality vs billing.

Priya: For billing I'd prefer option (1) with transparent invoices displaying requested vs used quality. We can gamma-correct pricing so small upgrades don't blow up cost.

Tej: Observability: add per-request fields to trace: requested_budget, used_lane, cache_fingerprint, fidelity_switches. We'll need tests to estimate quality degradation curves per workload so we can translate budget->expected nLL or Rouge drop.

Vikram: One more tricky bit: model version rollouts. If a new checkpoint has different quant sensitivity we must version lane_fingerprint semantics. Suggest include `profile_version` in cache metadata and disallow cross-version reuse unless compatibility table says ok.

Carol: Action items:
- Vikram + Tej: prototype lane_fingerprint in KV cache and a small shim to enforce compatibility (canary first)
- Priya: draft billing proposal (budget-based base price + used-credits reconciliation) and shared examples
- Carol: update RFC doc with API surface and response headers, add opt-in semantics for endpoints

ops-bot: Scheduled canary deploy window: 7190002000-7190005600 for quant-lane cache shim. Will post rollout checklist in #eng-releases :robot_face:

Tej: ack. I'll add unit tests for batch grouping and a sim that replays traffic with mixed budgets.

Priya: I'll sync with sales on the commercial constraints — want to avoid surprise charges for customers using PLG free-tier.

Vikram: FYI: rough perf estimate — switching lanes mid-sequence adds ~1-2ms per switch for KV boundary management. Will profile.

Carol: thanks team — this follow-up covered the major interface+ops tradeoffs. I'll push a short doc update and tag reviewers.
